author: a. l. cardenas
title: Nevada Wolf Pack teams prepare for final regular season contests and upcoming championships
text:
The Nevada Wolf Pack athletic teams are concluding their regular seasons this week, as announced on April 13, ahead of the Mountain West Championships. Baseball, softball, and track and field squads are set to compete on the road while both men’s and women’s tennis will finish their schedules before heading into postseason play.
This week holds importance for the Wolf Pack as several teams vie for strong finishes in conference standings. The baseball team is positioned just a half-game behind New Mexico in the Mountain West race at the halfway point of the season. Softball remains tied with UNLV for second place in its conference with nine games left.
Baseball will first play a non-conference game against Saint Mary’s before facing New Mexico in Albuquerque from April 17-19. Nevada enters these matchups following a series win over San José State and is currently tied with Air Force for second place in conference play.
Softball will host Pacific on Tuesday before traveling to Colorado State for three games starting Friday evening. The team’s recent performance has placed them firmly in contention for a bye through the championship play-in round.
Men’s tennis hosts Grand Canyon University at McArthur Tennis Center on Friday to close out its regular season. The team will then prepare to face top-seeded Utah State at next week’s Credit Union 1 Mountain West Championships in Las Vegas. Meanwhile, women’s tennis plays two away matches this week: Monday against San José State and Friday versus UNLV after recently defeating Fresno State at home.
Track and field athletes are set to compete at both the Bryan Clay Invitational in Azusa and Mt. SAC Relays in Walnut, California. These meets represent key opportunities as competitors aim to secure NCAA qualifying marks ahead of postseason events.
